Subject: Subprocessor onboarding: CloudLogix delegation & DPA evidence

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for taking this on. We are adding a downstream subprocessor (LogStream Inc) that will handle aggregated telemetry and short-term log retention for our managed connector to Redwood. Per your onboarding checklist we wanted to surface: scope of processing, subvendor chain, access model, and the DPA evidence you need.

Quick summary:
- Subprocessor: LogStream Inc (EU-based) — collects aggregated telemetry for 7 days, no PII stored.
- Sub-subprocessors: CDN provider (EdgeCache LLC) and analytics engine (DataPulse).
- Access model: SRE-level access for support (role-based, time-limited jumpbox sessions), API keys with rotation.
- Retention: 7 days aggregated logs; separate debug dumps retained up to 30 days for incident response (encrypted at rest).

Attached: CloudLogix_DPA.pdf (our current DPA), CloudLogix-SOC2-summary.pdf (attestation summary). Also attaching a matrix (cloudlogix-subproc-matrix.csv) that maps which subprocessor does what.

Can you confirm whether Redwood requires: (1) a signed flow-down Annex for LogStream, (2) DocuSign signature from cloudlogix procurement, and (3) any additional technical evidence beyond SOC2 (e.g., privileged access logs, jumpbox session records)?

We’re aiming to go-live for the integration week of Oct 4; if you need anything earlier, happy to jump on a quick call.

Thanks,
Adam
Adam Cole
Head of Integrations, CloudLogix
adam@cloudlogix.com

Hi Adam — thanks for the summary and the attachments. A few clarifying questions up front so we can route this quickly:

1) Can you confirm whether LogStream will be able to access request payloads that include user-generated content? You note "no PII," but we need a firm affirmation that payloads are strictly telemetry (hashes/metrics only).

2) For sub-subprocessors (EdgeCache, DataPulse) do you have flow-down language already in place, or will Redwood need to be in a direct flow-down with them?

3) For privileged access, please confirm: temporary admin sessions are logged in a syslog with session IDs and stored for 90 days? If not, provide how jumpbox sessions are audited.

On process: Legal and Procurement will want an order form amendment or an updated Order Form line item that references the subcontracting/flow-down. I've cc'd Laura (Legal) and Karthik (Procurement) to weigh in on contract language and billing impact.

If you can provide the signed SOC2 report (redacted ok), the DPA PDF you attached, and the matrix, that will help. If you prefer, supply a DocuSign link for the flow-down Annex and we can route the signature internally — our legal team prefers DocuSign records.

Proposed next step: 30-min call tomorrow 9am PT with Adam + Tessa + Laura to confirm scope and redline path. Does that work?

Best,

Team — summary and legal ask below. Forwarding back to Adam for confirmation on the few open items.

Summary of legal items to close before we accept LogStream as an authorized subprocessor:
1) Flow-down Annex: we require a signed Flow-Down Annex executed by CloudLogix and LogStream (template attached on request). Annex must: (a) bind the subprocessor to Redwood-equivalent obligations for confidentiality, security measures, and retention limits; (b) include audit cooperation language.
2) DPA Evidence: prefer SOC2 Type II report (redacted acceptable) plus the SOC2 bridge letter for the most recent period OR a compensating control narrative with session logging screenshots.
3) Order Form amendment: Procurement to include an explicit line referencing "Subprocessor delegation" and reference the DPA Annex by version/date. We will not accept a verbal-only flow-down.
4) Contract language: propose the following short clause (suggested insertion into MSA/Annex):
   "Vendor shall ensure that any subprocessors engaged to process Customer Data implement and maintain the same technical and organizational measures as Vendor and shall flow down the obligations of confidentiality, data protection and audit cooperation in a written annex signed by the subprocessor."

Escalation path: If CloudLogix cannot provide a signed annex for LogStream we will require a time-boxed mitigation plan (no more than 30 days from proposed go-live) and a compensating control such as isolated tenant routing and elevated monitoring. Procurement/Eng must approve the mitigation.

Action items for Adam / CloudLogix: please (A) provide SOC2 report or bridge letter, (B) provide signed Flow-Down Annex or DocuSign path and (C) confirm pricing/Order Form amendment completion.

I will prepare a short redline for the Flow-Down Annex and share to the thread by EOD tomorrow. Priyom/Rishi — please flag any additional security or legal controls we should require.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
